title: No Silver Bullet: Essence and Accidents of Software Engineering
summary: Brooks argues that better tools remove implementation overhead while the harder work remains specifying, designing and validating a complex system; he favors reuse, rapid prototypes, incremental development and skilled designers.
takeaways: Better languages and tools reduce accidental difficulty; deciding what a system should do and how its parts fit remains essential work.
Prototypes clarify requirements, and a running system grown incrementally makes feedback and backtracking easier.
The paper argues for steady improvement through several approaches, while questioning promises of a single tenfold breakthrough.

title: FairPrune: Achieving Fairness Through Pruning for Dermatological Disease Diagnosis
authors: Yawen Wu, Dewen Zeng, Xiaowei Xu, Yiyu Shi, Jingtong Hu
summary: Prunes the weights that matter much more to the better-served demographic group than to the other, shrinking the accuracy gap in skin-disease classifiers while overall accuracy stays close to the original.
takeaways: Fairness does not have to cost much accuracy.
Removing parameters that help the privileged group but contribute little to the unprivileged group narrows the performance gap.
Pruning can act as a fairness mechanism, not only as compression; a smaller model comes as a byproduct.

title: DiaMond: Dementia Diagnosis with Multi-Modal Vision Transformers Using MRI and PET
authors: Yitong Li, Morteza Ghahremani, Youssef Wally, Christian Wachinger
summary: A pure vision-transformer model that fuses MRI and PET through self-attention branches, a thresholded bi-attention branch and RegBN normalization, improving Alzheimer's prediction and AD vs. FTD differential diagnosis.
takeaways: Bi-attention with a threshold keeps only strong MRI to PET similarities, giving a cleaner cross-modal signal.
RegBN removes the part of one modality's features explained by the other, so each branch carries unique information.
Pure ViT fusion beats PET-only and CNN or fusion baselines, including on the harder AD vs. FTD differential diagnosis.

title: Beyond Self-Attention: Deformable Large Kernel Attention for Medical Image Segmentation
authors: Reza Azad, Leon Niggemeier, Michael Hüttemann, Amirhossein Kazerouni, Ehsan Khodapanah Aghdam, Yury Velichko, Ulaş Bağcı, Dorit Merhof
summary: Deformable large kernel attention (D-LKA) pairs large convolution kernels with deformable sampling, capturing global context and irregular organ shapes at lower cost than self-attention, in 2D and 3D segmentation networks.
takeaways: Large kernels give broad context; deformable sampling bends the receptive field around irregular shapes and boundaries.
The 3D variant uses inter-slice continuity instead of segmenting volumes slice by slice.
My replication came within about 4 Dice points of the reported 2D result and about 2 on 3D pancreas, but training needs a lot of memory and time.
